newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran affirms foreigners safe despite row with EU.
newsitem.headline: Iran affirms foreigners safe despite row with EU.

text.p: Iran said on Tuesday it was committed to protecting foreigners as protests continued against a German court verdict accusing Iranian leaders of ordering political killings.
Iranian riot police guarded the German embassy in Tehran, where they arrested students trying to attack the compound on Monday in the first violent protest since Thursday's verdict.

"Iran is committed to protecting the lives of foreign citizens just like its own citizens and our people are not a threat to anybody either," parliamentary speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri said in remarks reported by state-run Tehran radio.

"Iran stopped the students from attacking the German embassy because of its pledges and commitment to international rules," added Nateq-Nouri, tipped as a front runner in Iran's May presidential elections.
Bonn has said it had no reason to doubt Iranian assurances the 530 Germans in Iran were safe.

The radio carried reports from two dozen cities across Iran where it said marches were held to protest against the verdict that accused Iranian leaders of ordering the killing of four Kurdish opposition figures in Berlin in 1992 -- the first such judicial finding against Iran since the 1979 revolution.
Witnesses said police outside the barricaded German embassy in a busy central Tehran avenue barred pedestrians from walking along the pavement.

Iranian media said veterans disabled by Iraqi chemical attacks in the 1980-88 war between the two neighbours would march on the embassy on Wednesday to protest at the verdict and against German firms which allegedly provided chemicals to Iraq.
But residents said the hardline Islamist group Ansar-e Hizbollah (Supporters of the Party of God) cancelled without explanation a march they had announced for Tuesday.

Iranians have marched on the embassy three times since Thursday's verdict, but Monday's was the first violence. Iran's official news agency IRNA said police arrested some Islamist students, whose spokesman warned "they would seize the embassy unless the German government make a formal apology to the Iranian nation and retreat from hostility against Iran".
Iran -- fighting U.S. sanctions and keen to preserve links with Europe -- has repeatedly denied any role in the Berlin killings, which it blames on fighting between opposition groups.

European Union member states, except Greece, said they would recall ambassadors for consultations and Iran said it would reciprocate. But both Bonn and Tehran indicated they did not want a total diplomatic break.
EU states have resisted U.S. pressure for sanctions on Iran, which Washington accuses of sponsoring terrorism. Tehran denies the charges.

"It is clear that Europe will not join America's trade ban against Iran and the fire of diplomatic disputes will die down earlier that expected because of Iran's just stance," Tehran radio said in a commentary.
Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Monday some EU states had assured Tehran withdrawing ambassadors was not meant to damage ties with Iran.

Iranian newspapers blasted Germany on Tuesday over the verdict, with the daily Akhbar carrying a cartoon of Adolf Hitler covering his face with a mask resembling German Chancellor Helmut Kohl. "Hitler is not dead," the caption said.
